title: Week 11 availability report does not exist yet
what_the_official_record_says: The week-11 injury endpoint returns the week-10 report (page title and body heading both say Week 10, and the week selector stops at WEEK 10), and both clubs' game-centre blocks say the report is not available at this time. No week-11 designation can be published, so P-03 has no events to fire on and REQ-53 stays blocked.
what_we_do_about_it: Re-read the endpoint on the league's own publication days; the capture workflow records an empty capture rather than skipping it, so the gap is visible instead of looking like an all-clear.

title: Chargers at Ravens published with no score
what_the_official_record_says: At retrieval (2026-11-17T00:39Z, 36 minutes before kickoff) the fixture had not been played. Scores are blank in the results feed and the standings row for both clubs excludes it, which is exactly why games played differs by club (LAC 8, BAL 9).
what_we_do_about_it: Score this row from the final week page on the next read; the reconciliation check will fail loudly if anyone fills it early.

title: Carried-forward results feed keys two clubs by a different code than the standings page
what_the_official_record_says: The feed uses LAR and ARI while the league standings page uses LA and AZ. Joining the two by code silently drops nine games for each club (18 club-games). The league-wide totals still balanced, so the aggregate check passed while one club's record was short a whole game: only the per-club reconciliation caught it.
what_we_do_about_it: Explicit alias map applied at read time, the alias is recorded per row, and the reconciliation check now passes 32 of 32. Every desk that trained on that feed without an alias map is affected.

title: An earlier desk's blocking flag says no market price of any kind exists in this repo
what_the_official_record_says: It does: data/decision-desk/raw/games.csv.gz holds 7548 games from 1999 to 2026, of which 7439 carry a spread and total and 5458 carry both moneylines; 163 of the 272 2026 rows are priced. What is missing is not a price but a price in an admitted source class with open and close separately.
what_we_do_about_it: Re-worded as a policy gate rather than a data gap, and it is now S-01/S-02 on the suggestions page where a one-day audit decides it.

title: Baltimore's quarterbacks were repeatedly described as placed on injured reserve
what_the_official_record_says: The dated league register read here contains no such move: November rows run 11/16 down to 11/07 with no Baltimore row, and late-October rows run 10/31 down to 10/24 with the only Baltimore entry being a defensive lineman placed on reserve 10/24. What the league does publish is a report that the starting quarterback is out 6 to 9 weeks with a thumb injury, which is a medical status, not a reserve-list event. Baltimore did trade for a quarterback on 11/06.
what_we_do_about_it: Do not treat this as an IR event. Absence is also not proof of health because the month pages stop after about 25 rows (CU-F06), so the claim needs a complete paginated sweep before it can be settled either way.

title: The transactions register pages are capped
what_the_official_record_says: Both month pages read here returned about 25 rows and stopped mid-month. A single fetch per month therefore cannot support the 32-team sweep, and it cannot support a negative claim about a player's roster status.
what_we_do_about_it: The capture job must paginate and record the row count per page; a sweep that stops at 25 rows must be reported as incomplete rather than empty.

title: Three Lions game-status cells were blank on the site
what_the_official_record_says: The official report now carries a designation for all three: Kerby Joseph Out, Cade Mays Out, D.J. Reed Out, each with Did Not Participate In Practice. This session's read is the second dated read of that report and it agrees with the first.
what_we_do_about_it: Nothing left to populate; the rows are published with the clock time of the read that confirmed them.

title: Two reads of one weekly report, 49 hours apart, differ by nothing
what_the_official_record_says: 147 field values compared across 49 rows: 0 changed. After the report's own deadline the file is static, so a daily capture between Friday and kickoff mostly duplicates rows and can create the illusion of a series.
what_we_do_about_it: Capture on publication days, then capture the two artefacts that actually change late (transactions, and the inactives list once it exists), and treat the report as a step function.

title: The fetcher truncated one club's injury table mid-row
what_the_official_record_says: Kansas City's sixth line was cut off in the retrieval, so Patrick Mahomes' row is not published at all rather than guessed. Five complete rows are published with a PARTIAL coverage flag.
what_we_do_about_it: Per-club row-count pins in the capture job, which is the concrete form of the drift alarm requirement.

title: Price data and the ordering rule
what_the_official_record_says: The brief says the price-data policy must be decided before any backtest is published. That decision is open, so nothing in this desk is called a backtest: the residual column is typed and empty and the capability audit reports only what the corpus contains.
what_we_do_about_it: Record a one-line decision in the repo (admit the third-party class for backtesting, or buy a licensed feed, or stay official-only).

title: Public layer currently contains raw row-level captures
what_the_official_record_says: An earlier desk's public page renders 700 raw club depth rows, while the brief's own rule is to keep raw row-level data in a private store until the terms are read.
what_we_do_about_it: Either record the exception explicitly or move the raw tables behind the private layer; both are cheaper than leaving eight desks inconsistent.

title: The landing page still shows a two-week-old state
what_the_official_record_says: The repo-root index describes eight research candidates and a 2026-11-02 review date while the site now carries eight NFL desks and this session's 2026-11-17 read. No page indexes them.
what_we_do_about_it: An integration session publishes one index naming every desk with its capture date; this desk's files are deliberately not hand-edited into the shared root.

title: decision-desk workflow fails its rebuild check on every PR
what_the_official_record_says: Logged by two earlier sessions and still open: the committed outputs under data/decision-desk do not reproduce from their own build, so the check that is meant to prove reproducibility reports failure regardless of the PR.
what_we_do_about_it: Owned by the decision-desk sessions; untouched here. Any fix must regenerate rather than hand-patch the outputs.

title: Two corpora are both called the record
what_the_official_record_says: The verified 2026 official record is 149 finals plus 1 unplayed game; the third-party snap corpus covers 136 games for weeks 1 to 9. A gate that counts games must name which corpus it counted, or a sample-size threshold gets met by the wrong file.
what_we_do_about_it: The engine prints both counts on every build and every table names its source class.

title: The originator is not yet better than a naive baseline
what_the_official_record_says: On six walk-forward weeks the two total estimators split the weeks 3 and 3 and the league-average total beat both in two of them (9.38 and 10.99 mean absolute error). Publishing that is the point of the control rows.
what_we_do_about_it: Keep both estimators and the control published; do not promote any strategy on this evidence.
